newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bear Stearns reinitiates Mexican bank coverage.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns reinitiates Mexican bank coverage.

text.p: Bear Stearns said on Tuesday that it was reinitiating coverage of the Mexican banking sector, and announced two new ratings.
A report written by analyst Alberto Sanchez started coverage of Banca Serfin with an "unattractive" rating while it started Banorte with an "attractive" rating.
It also included "three follow-ups of existing ratings for Banacci (neutral), Bancomer (neutral) and Quadrum (neutral)," Bear Stearns said.

Bear Stearns said the report included a new way of looking at banks called the franchise ratio, which "values one percent market share of deposits at each bank compared to the relative wealth of each country in Latin America".
"This ratio indicates that Mexican banks are significantly undervalued if looked at isolated from other problems," Bear Stearns said.

The report said it expected new accounting rules to be introduced in 1997 and that these, together with other difficulties facing Mexican banks, would have a "significantly negative" effect next year.
"Going forward we continue to see a stabilization of asset-quality ratios as the economy rebounds and consolidation of the banking system progresses," it said.

"However, net interest margins should remain relatively low due to deposit competition and increased interbank funding, so the clean-up process of balance sheets (provisions and charge-offs) may be delayed well into 1997."
